outcome: One consistent firewall standard across every site gives the operator a security posture it can demonstrate and defend.
overview: A remote oil and gas plant runs its own perimeter, often installed years apart across several sites and maintained by whoever was available. Standardising it means migrating live firewalls without interrupting production, which is why this engagement ran as phased test-environment deployments before anything moved in anger. Redington and partner Mannai Trading upgraded and migrated the existing firewalls to FortiGate across multiple sites, giving the operator one perimeter standard and one rule base to review. This outcome is backed by a published, named-customer account of the engagement.

benefits.text: One perimeter standard across sites replaces devices installed and configured years apart
benefits.limits: The published reference describes one named customer engagement. It is evidence that Redington has delivered this, and it is not a performance figure that transfers to the next customer

benefits.text: Migration is rehearsed in a test environment before any production site is touched
benefits.limits: Rehearsal reduces cutover risk but lengthens the schedule; at a remote plant the schedule is set by site access, not by engineering

benefits.text: A single rule base can be reviewed, so permissive rules become visible
benefits.limits: The same operating system runs on the appliance, as a virtual machine and in cloud, so the capability claim survives a form-factor change; the throughput figure behind it does not, and must be re-sized per form factor

residency: Appliances, management and logs remain within the operator’s own estate at the plant and in the corporate data centre

notFor.situation: A single-site operator with a current, supported perimeter
notFor.why: The value here is standardisation across sites; with one site there is nothing to standardise

notFor.situation: Sites where no maintenance window can be obtained within the programme horizon
notFor.why: A live firewall migration needs a window, and a rehearsed cutover needs a scheduled one

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner; the referenced engagement was delivered with partner Mannai Trading · Duration: 12–20 weeks depending on site count and access windows
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with a replacement term appropriate to remote-site logistics; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Review — device inventory, rule-base export and analysis, per-site traffic measurement
2) Rehearse — test environment built, cutover runbook validated against it
3) Migrate — sites cut over one at a time on the runbook, with on-site rollback available
4) Standardise and hand over — central management holding one policy set, operations handed over
deliverables: Each site cutover completes inside its agreed window or is rolled back to the original device within it
Central management holds one policy set from which every site’s configuration derives
The estate-wide log store receives events from every migrated site
effort: 12–20 weeks depending on site count and access windows
languages: English delivery; Arabic site documentation on request
